hypothesis: Richard Wyckoff's 'spring' pattern: within an accumulation range (sideways consolidation), price makes a brief failed breakdown below support on light volume (a shakeout of weak-handed sellers), then reclaims support on expanding volume, signaling absorption by smart-money accumulation rather than genuine distribution. Per TradingSim's explicit mechanical rule: 'Setup: an accumulation zone at least two weeks old, a break below support on light volume, then a reclaim of support on expanding volume. Entry: the close back above support, or the next open if it opens above support. Stop: just below the spring low. Target: the top of the zone first, then the height of the zone projected above it.' Operationalized on daily bars: accumulation zone = range_window-day period with rolling range width <= range_width_pct of its midpoint; support = the zone's rolling low; spring bar = close/low dips below support on below-average volume; reclaim = within reclaim_window bars, close back above support on above-average volume -> long entry; exit at the zone's rolling high (target), a stop below the spring low, or a max_hold_days time-stop. Source: https://www.tradingsim.com/blog/wyckoff-method-trading ('Entry and Exit Rules for Wyckoff Trades' section, read in-browser). First Wyckoff-family strategy in this repo -- a genuinely new pattern construction (volume-confirmed failed-breakdown-then-reclaim inside a detected consolidation range) distinct from all prior breakout/mean-reversion/divergence constructions already tested.
